cain.chase.escaped.text: Abel got home to his father and mother. You are a good person: you did not want to kill Abel, and that is good. But it did not happen that way. Play it again as the Bible tells it.

cain.command.0.text: Cain, Abel. Bring me an offering, each of you, from the work of your hands.

cain.command.1.text: I will bring the fruit of my field.

cain.command.2.text: And I, the firstlings of my flock.

cain.fear.0.text: Cain? What are you doing with that?

cain.field.0.text: Abel. Come with me, let us go out to the field.

cain.herd.0.text: Come, boy! Bring them in to the fold.

cain.npc.adam.after.0.text: The LORD looked on your brother's offering. Do not let your heart grow dark.

cain.npc.adam.after.1.text: Anger is a heavy thing to carry, son. Put it down.

cain.npc.adam.after.2.text: Where is your brother? He should be home before the evening.

cain.npc.adam.before.0.text: I worked the ground by the sweat of my brow. Now my sons work it with me.

cain.npc.adam.before.1.text: Bring the LORD your best, my son.

cain.npc.adam.before.2.text: We could not go back to the garden. But the LORD has not left us.

cain.npc.adam.before.3.text: Cain keeps the field, Abel keeps the sheep. Each has his work.

cain.npc.eve.after.0.text: Your face has fallen, Cain. What is it?

cain.npc.eve.after.1.text: Make peace with your brother before the sun goes down.

cain.npc.eve.after.2.text: Is Abel with you? I have kept his bread warm.

cain.npc.eve.before.0.text: I have gotten a man from the LORD. And then another. My two sons.

cain.npc.eve.before.1.text: The pot is almost ready. Go on, do your work first.

cain.npc.eve.before.2.text: Take care of your brother, Cain.

cain.npc.eve.before.3.text: The tunics the LORD made us still keep us warm.

cain.rebuke.0.text: Why are you angry? Why has your face fallen?

cain.rebuke.1.text: If you do well, will you not be accepted? If not, sin lies at the door. It wants you, but you must rule over it.

cain.scripture.born.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD.

cain.scripture.firstlings.text: And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.

cain.scripture.keeper.text: And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

cain.scripture.mark.text: And the LORD set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.

cain.scripture.nod.text: And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.

cain.scripture.respect.text: And the LORD had respect unto Abel and to his offering: but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.

cain.scripture.slew.text: And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.

cain.scripture.wroth.text: And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.

cain.where.1.text: I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?

cain.where.2.text: What have you done? Your brother's blood cries to me from the ground. You will be a wanderer on the earth.

creation.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

m02_command.0.text: Eat freely from every tree — but not from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. The day you eat of it, you will surely die.

m02_forbidden.0.text: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

m03_intro.0.text: It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.

m04_wake.0.text: This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

m05_intro.0.text: Let us gather fruit — from every tree but one.

m05_share.0.text: Every tree is a gift — all but the one in the midst.

m06_serpent.0.text: Did God really say, “You shall not eat of any tree of the garden”?

m06_serpent.1.text: We may eat from the trees, but not from the one in the midst, or we will die.

m06_serpent.2.text: You will not surely die. God knows your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.

m08_answer.0.text: I heard your voice and was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid.

m08_answer.1.text: Did you eat from the tree I commanded you not to eat from?

m08_answer.2.text: The woman you gave me — she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.

m08_answer.3.text: What is this that you have done?

m08_answer.4.text: The serpent deceived me, and I ate.

m09_adam.0.text: The ground is cursed because of you; it will bring thorns and thistles. Dust you are, and to dust you will return.

m09_serpent.0.text: You are cursed; on your belly you will go. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.

m09_woman.0.text: In pain you will bear children. You will long for your husband, and he will rule over you.

m10_intro.0.text: The man now knows good and evil. He must not take from the tree of life and live forever.

scripture.gen2_15.text: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

scripture.gen2_20.text: And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.

scripture.gen2_22.text: And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.

scripture.gen3_21.text: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them.

scripture.gen3_24.text: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

scripture.gen3_6.text: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.
